title: Career Roadmap · Nursery Technician
summary: A Nursery Technician propagates and maintains plants, manages growing media and irrigation, monitors pests and diseases, and prepares healthy seedlings, saplings and ornamental plants for sale or transplantation.

facts.Current degree: Diploma in Horticulture / Agriculture or relevant nursery-production training

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Agriculture or Science with Biology; entry requirements depend on the programme.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Botany, biology, soil science, plant nutrition and basic chemistry.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: Check the current eligibility rules for the chosen diploma or certificate.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Seed germination, plant propagation, nursery irrigation, potting and greenhouse management.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Plant identification, careful observation, hygiene, recordkeeping and practical work.

items.text: Diploma in Horticulture → Nursery production, plant propagation and ornamental plant care.
Diploma in Agriculture → Seedling production, crop establishment and farm operations.
Diploma / certificate in nursery management → Practical nursery operations, subject to provider recognition.
B.Sc. Horticulture → Broader technical roles in nursery management, landscaping and plant production.
B.Sc. Agriculture → Crop production, agricultural extension and related technical opportunities.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Course titles and eligibility vary by institution. Verify recognition, practical training and whether the qualification is accepted by your intended employer.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Plant identification, growing media, seed germination, potting and nursery hygiene.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Cutting, grafting, layering, irrigation, fertilisation and pest monitoring.

blocks.label: Year 3, if applicable
blocks.text: Greenhouse operations, inventory, nursery costing and customer orders.

blocks.label: Final stage
blocks.text: Practical project, work experience and job preparation.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Seed-germination comparison • Cutting-propagation success tracker • Nursery watering schedule • Seedling health and inventory register.

blocks.label: Government / research
blocks.text: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, agricultural universities, KVKs and government nurseries.

blocks.label: Private
blocks.text: Commercial plant nurseries, landscaping firms, greenhouse operators, tissue-culture labs and garden centres.

blocks.label: Ideal exposure
blocks.text: Seed propagation, grafting, plant health, irrigation systems and nursery stock management.

Training or internship availability depends on the organisation and programme; placements are not guaranteed. ICAR lists horticulture research institutes and agricultural universities on its official website.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Academic transcripts, relevant subject prerequisites, English proficiency where required, funding evidence and student-visa documents. Diploma credit transfer varies by institution.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: Nursery Technician, Horticulture Technician, Greenhouse Assistant, Plant Propagation Technician, Nursery Team Leader.

Experience, practical skills and local work-authorisation rules affect eligibility. Employment and visa sponsorship are not guaranteed.
